strengths: Strong empirical results: achieves up to 27.6× speedup with minimal accuracy loss (1-2%) across multiple benchmarks and model architectures
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: includes ablations on block size, confidence threshold, generation length, and comparisons with fixed token-per-step baselines
Empirical justification: KV activation similarity heatmaps (Figure 3) provide clear evidence for the caching approximation
Effective technique combination: the two proposed methods complement each other well, with synergistic speedups
Theoretical contribution: Theorem 1 formally characterizes conditions for parallel decoding safety with rigorous convergence bounds
Practical applicability: training-free method that applies to existing Diffusion LLMs without modification
Thorough ablations: careful analysis of design choices with clear presentation via figures and tables
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual contributions (block-wise caching, confidence-based selection) are straightforward adaptations of existing ideas with incremental innovation
Incomplete baseline comparisons: missing experimental comparison with Block Diffusion [1] (cited concurrent work), other Diffusion LLM acceleration techniques, and AR models with optimization methods
Narrow experimental scope: evaluation limited to single batch size (unrealistic for deployment), one hardware type (A100 GPU), and only two masked diffusion models

Theoretical gaps: Theorem 1 assumes well-defined joint PMF that MDMs may not satisfy (acknowledged in Remark 1); worst-case bounds have limited practical relevance; critical condition (n+1)ε ≤ 1 lacks empirical verification
Insufficient approximation analysis: no characterization of how error accumulates across blocks; DualCache design (caching masked tokens) lacks clear justification; memory overhead not discussed
Hyperparameter selection: block size 32 and threshold 0.9 appear arbitrary with limited guidance for practitioners on how to select parameters for new models/tasks
Qualitative evaluation insufficient: case study limited to one arithmetic example; no human evaluation or semantic similarity metrics; quality degradation only measured via accuracy
Reproducibility concerns: code not provided for review; implementation details missing; hyperparameter selection process not documented

strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: addresses real efficiency gap in diffusion LLMs lacking KV cache support and suffering from parallel decoding quality degradation
Strong empirical results: achieves up to 27.6× speedup with minimal accuracy loss (±1-2 points) across multiple models and benchmarks

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: systematic testing on LLaDA, Dream, LLaDA-V across GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, MBPP, MathVista, MathVerse with detailed ablations on block size, thresholds, and prefill/generation lengths
Solid theoretical contribution: Theorem 1 formally justifies parallel decoding with high-confidence tokens, including tight equivalence bounds and comprehensive divergence analysis (KL, L_p, TV)
Training-free approach: practical advantage enabling immediate deployment without model retraining
Excellent presentation: clear writing, convincing visualizations (Figure 3 heatmaps), thorough proofs, and extensive appendices demonstrating rigor
Generalizes across model architectures and task types: speedups consistent across different models (LLaDA/Dream variants) and problem domains (math, code, vision-language)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: block-wise KV cache and confidence-thresholding are incremental adaptations of straightforward ideas rather than significant algorithmic advances

Theory-practice gap in Theorem 1: assumes well-defined joint p_θ violating MDM properties (acknowledged but implications unclear); tight bound ε≤1/(n+1) and connection to practical threshold τ=0.9 not rigorously justified

KV cache approximation lacks rigor: no formal error quantification despite 'negligible performance drop' claims; multimodal LLaDA-V requires completely different strategy (full blocks + refresh) due to >8% accuracy degradation with small blocks, indicating fundamental limitations

Batch size scalability limitations (Section C.5): both PrefixCache and LLaDA plateau after batch size 8 while autoregressive LLaMA scales smoothly, severely limiting high-throughput deployment applicability

Hyperparameter brittleness: cache block size (Figure 4), confidence threshold, and factor require tuning with high sensitivity; different strategies needed for different models; limited principled guidance for practitioners on hyperparameter selection

Incomplete baseline comparisons: missing comparisons to Block Diffusion [1] and other diffusion acceleration techniques; no comparison to speculative decoding or generic inference acceleration methods
Limited model coverage: only tested on masked diffusion models (LLaDA, Dream); no evaluation on SEDD, CTMC, or other discrete diffusion approaches; generalization unclear
Statistical rigor: no confidence intervals or significance tests; some accuracy changes (1-2 points) within potential noise margins; missing multi-run analysis
Confidence metric unexplored: uses max softmax without ablation; no investigation of alternative confidence functions or their impact on theoretical guarantees
Algorithm and evaluation details: unclear specification in Algorithm 1 (line 6); missing latency percentiles and memory consumption analysis; some results relegated to appendix

strengths: Addresses practical efficiency problem in emerging diffusion LLM models with training-free approach
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (LLaDA, Dream, LLaDA-V) and diverse benchmarks with extensive ablation studies
Well-motivated technical approach with empirical observation of high KV activation similarity (Figure 3) and clear identification of parallel decoding degradation root cause
Impressive speedup results (up to 27.6×) with minimal accuracy loss (1-2 points), demonstrated across text and multimodal tasks
Theorem 1 provides formal theoretical justification for confidence-based parallel decoding with explicit divergence bounds
Clear presentation with informative visualizations and detailed appendix including qualitative analysis
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: KV caching is well-established; confidence-based selection is incremental over LLaDA's top-K approach
Theoretical contribution is modest: Theorem 1 assumes well-defined joint PMF that MDMs may not satisfy; worst-case bounds are loose and restrictive condition (n+1)ε≤1 may not hold in practice
KV Cache approximation lacks depth: fundamentally breaks down for multimodal LLaDA-V (accuracy drops >8% with small blocks, requiring different refresh strategy), suggesting unaddressed limitations
Scalability concerns underexplored: LLaDA throughput plateaus at batch size ~8 (Figure 9), severely limiting practical deployment; compute-bound nature of diffusion models acknowledged but not solved

Experimental design issues: headline '27.6×' speedup uses atypical conditions (8-shot + 1024 tokens); modest 5-8× speedups for standard 256-token generation; limited batch-size analysis; weak baselines (mostly method variants, no comparison with other acceleration techniques)

Confidence-based decoding lacks principled design: threshold (0.9) appears ad-hoc with non-trivial sensitivity (Figure 5); 'always unmask max confidence' fallback is a hack; factor-based strategy trades 1-3% accuracy for throughput gains without clear characterization
Insufficient baseline comparisons: only 2 AR models in one setting (Figure 1a); no comparison with other acceleration methods (quantization, pruning, distillation) or alternative inference approaches
Limited analysis of failure modes and accuracy-efficiency trade-offs: no investigation of task/token-type sensitivity; missing characterization of when method is not recommended
